items.title: Stress professionnel élevé chez les employées du secteur privé en Tunisie
items.description: Une étude scientifique menée entre mai 2018 et décembre 2019, auprès de 1 042 femmes ayant une moyenne d’âge de 33,3 ans, employées dans des entreprises affiliées au groupement de médecine du travail du gouvernorat de Sousse, a mis en évidence l’impact significatif du stress professionnel sur la qualité de vie et la santé mentale des femmes travaillant dans le secteur privé en Tunisie. Pour parer à cette situation, l’étude préconise le renforcement des mécanismes de soutien et de gestion du stress au sein de l’environnement de travail. Les résultats, présentés par l'agence Tap, mettent en évidence un niveau élevé de stress professionnel chez 14,4 % des femmes, tandis que 11,3 % d’entre elles souffraient d’un stress professionnel associé à un isolement social. En ce qui concerne la qualité de vie, l’indice moyen de santé physique perçue chez les participantes s’est établi à 38,83 points, contre 43,19 points pour l’indice de santé mentale ; à titre de comparaison, une situation normale correspond à un indice compris entre 50 et 70 points, tandis que la situation idéale atteint 100 points. La santé mentale est apparue comme l’aspect le plus affecté, l’étude ayant relevé une détérioration de la qualité de vie mentale chez 86,8 % des participantes. L’étude conclut que le stress professionnel constitue un facteur déterminant de la qualité de vie perçue chez les femmes travaillant dans le secteur privé en Tunisie, en raison de ses répercussions sur leur santé mentale et physique ainsi que sur l’équilibre entre leur vie professionnelle et personnelle. Elle préconise la mise en place de mesures de soutien psychosocial et de gestion du stress professionnel au sein des entreprises, ainsi que l’amélioration des conditions de travail, afin de favoriser le bien-être des travailleuses et d’atténuer les effets négatifs du stress lié au travail. I. B. L’article Stress professionnel élevé chez les employées du secteur privé en Tunisie est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

Taekwondo goes to school as GTF launches five-region youth campaign
items.description: About 500 schoolchildren from 10 private schools in the Ashanti Region have participated in the launch of a Ghana Taekwondo Federation (GTF) campaign aimed at taking the sport into schools and communities across five regions. The Regional Taekwondo Awareness Campaign, launched in Kumasi, will initially cover the Ashanti, Northern, Upper West, Bono and Central regions. The initiative, held under the theme “Promoting Taekwondo Awareness, Discipline, Fitness and Youth Development,” seeks to increase access to the sport, identify young talent early and promote discipline, physical fitness, self-defence and confidence among children. GTF President Frederick Lartey Otu said the campaign represents a broader approach to using Taekwondo as a tool for youth development. “The future of Taekwondo in Ghana lies not only in producing champions, but also in producing disciplined, responsible and confident young people.” He said the programme would create pathways for young athletes to progress from school and community programmes to regional and national competitions. Mr Lartey Otu also called for stronger collaboration among schools, parents, teachers, coaches, sports authorities and Taekwondo associations. “This programme requires partnership, commitment and collective responsibility.” The Executive Director of the Ghana National Council of Private Schools (GNACOPS), Obenfo Nana Kwasi Gyetuah, called for a rethink of the role of sports in Ghana’s education system. He said sports should not be treated simply as a co-curricular activity but as an important part of developing the whole child. “For too long, we have treated sports as something children do after the real learning is done. Sports teach discipline, focus, respect, resilience, teamwork and leadership. These are not extras. They are the very foundation of the transformed learner Ghana needs.” He urged schools and parents to give sports adequate time, space and support. The Ashanti Regional Director of the National Sports Authority (NSA), Nana Gyaama Dakwa, pledged the Directorate’s support for grassroots sports development and encouraged more schools to participate in Taekwondo. She said the sport could improve physical fitness and mental alertness while equipping children with self-defence skills. “When the kids know how to defend themselves, especially the ladies, I think it will be of much help to them.” The launch featured demonstrations by schoolchildren and Taekwondo practitioners, including Poomsae and self-defence techniques. The GTF National Executive Board also presented uniforms and equipment to the Ashanti Regional Taekwondo Association to support training and development. The event brought together school proprietors, teachers, parents, coaches, Taekwondo officials and representatives of the National Sports Authority and GNACOPS.

items.title: ‘It is possible to live together in dignity and peace’ — Pope
items.description: Pope Leo XIV said on Saturday it was possible to “live together in dignity and peace” as he met migrants in Paris, ahead of a giant open-air mass expected to gather hundreds of thousands of people on the iconic Champs Elysees. The first US pontiff is visiting France on a four-day trip as the European nation gears up for elections next year to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with the anti-immigration far right eyeing its best chance at the top job. On the second day of the first official papal visit to the European nation in 18 years, the leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics will lead the faithful in prayer from 3:00 pm (1300 GMT). Around 600,000 people were expected to attend the event at Place de la Concorde and along the adjoining Champs Elysees. President Emmanuel Macron will not attend the mass, but several presidential hopefuls, including far-right leader Marine Le Pen and centrist Edouard Philippe, have confirmed their attendance. Earlier Saturday the pope visited Maison Bakhita, an association supporting migrants and refugees. “I am pleased to begin this second day in Paris with you, in a house that bears witness to the whole city that it is possible to encounter one another and to live together in dignity and peace,” he said. He had been set to meet women and men, of Christian and Muslim faith, from Algeria, Belarus, Iraq and the Ivory Coast, the association had said, calling it a “message” in the run-up to elections. “The pope is coming to tell the French that, whatever our political convictions, we share a common humanity and a right to dignity,” association president Valerie Moniod has told reporters. The pope has called the treatment of migrants in the United States “extremely disrespectful” and said “we have to look for ways of treating people humanely.” Leo’s visit to France has stirred enthusiasm and spiritual fervour among the faithful. On Friday, an estimated 300,000 people came out to see the pontiff as he waved to the crowds from his popemobile on the way to the Notre Dame Cathedral. – AI warning – On Friday, Pope Leo stressed the need for ethics to avoid an AI-driven “paradise of machines” and, as war rages in Ukraine for a fifth year, urged France to remain a “tireless champion of peace”. On Friday night, he told young adults at a stadium outside the French capital that they were the “saints of France” and that the Church needed them. In a deeply secular country, only around five percent of France’s 69 million residents go to Catholic church services regularly, a survey found last year. But while the number of infants getting baptised has dwindled in recent years, more teenagers and adults are taking the plunge. After the mass in Paris, Pope Leo will head to Lourdes, a town in southwestern France where, according to Catholic tradition, the Virgin Mary appeared in a grotto in 1858 to a peasant girl. In Lourdes on Sunday, he will speak with seven victims of clerical sex abuse. A 2021 inquiry found that clergy or lay members of the Church had abused about 330,000 people as minors in France, over seven decades. In recent years, further accusations have emerged against charity icon Abbe Pierre and workers at a Catholic boarding school near Lourdes. For the last leg of his trip in Metz, on Monday, Leo is expected to make a speech about peace in Europe. items.title: The issues Mourinho is struggling to fix at Real Madrid
items.description: When Jose Mourinho walked back through the doors at Real Madrid this summer, 13 years had passed since he last left the club. He returned with a familiar reputation and enormous expectations, but facing a very different challenge. Mourinho was handed a three-year contract, with the club hoping he could restore stability and success after two trophyless seasons. Now, seven league matches into his second spell, some of the familiar tensions of last season have already resurfaced. Defeat by rivals Atletico Madrid has left supporters questioning Real Madrid’s consistency and Mourinho’s approach. The Portuguese coach now has plenty of time to consider his options during an unusually long three-week international break. Madrid do not play again until they host Villarreal on Saturday, 10 October – and travel to Barcelona two weeks later. Mourinho has concerns about the break, but it is an early opportunity to take stock and prepare for a run of fixtures that could tell us much more about the direction of his second spell at the Bernabeu. How have Real Madrid started? For Mourinho, the derby defeat at Atletico Madrid was a sobering reminder of the scale of the challenge he has taken on. Despite blaming much of the loss on two first-half decisions he felt went against his side – Cristian Romero escaping a red card for his studs-up challenge on Jude Bellingham and Lee Kang-in going unpunished for a similar challenge on Federico Valverde – the reality is that their performance was simply not good enough. It means Real Madrid sit fourth in La Liga, with defending champions Barcelona already six points ahead. They have won all seven of their league games, scoring 31 goals, with Raphinha already scoring 12 times. Atletico sit second and Real Betis third, both five points behind Hansi Flick’s side. The only time Real Madrid have overturned a six-point deficit to Barcelona at the top of La Liga was in Fabio Capello’s 2006-07 title triumph. What do Real Madrid need to improve? A clear issue from the defeat at Atletico was Madrid’s lack of control in midfield. Mourinho started Aurelien Tchouameni alongside Valverde, with Bellingham playing further forward. The pairing gave Madrid energy and defensive security, but they struggled to control the tempo or create enough from deeper areas. Bernardo Silva was introduced for the final eight minutes, but by then Madrid were already chasing the game. That presents Mourinho with an interesting selection decision. Against opponents who defend in a compact shape, Madrid may need more creativity and control from midfield. Silva’s ability to dictate the rhythm of a game makes him an obvious option, while Arda Guler offers another creative presence further forward. Mourinho doesn’t necessarily need to abandon the double pivot, but he does need to find a way for Real to have more control of matches. Get more from Mbappe and Vinicius Jr There is no shortage of individual attacking quality at Real Madrid. The problem is making it work consistently as a unit. Against Atletico, Madrid struggled to create clear chances. Kylian Mbappe was largely ineffective and hardly touched the ball, while Vinicius Jr was substituted shortly after Dean Huijsen’s red card early in the second half. Mourinho has three players, in Vinicius, Mbappe and Bellingham, capable of deciding matches on their own. Bellingham’s ability to carry the ball forward, arrive late in the box and link midfield with attack is another important part of Madrid’s attacking threat, but Mourinho needs to ensure the trio complement rather than crowd each other. Vinicius needs to rediscover the explosiveness and directness that makes him so difficult to defend, while Mbappe needs a greater supply of chances rather than being asked to create opportunities for himself. There is another attacking option Mourinho could turn to more often. Carlos Espi has already made an impression since joining the club, scoring the 90th-minute winner against Espanyol on his league debut before doing it again in stoppage time against Elche. The 21-year-old has therefore shown he can make an impact when given game time. With Madrid still working out how best to balance Vinicius, Mbappe and Bellingham, Espi offers Mourinho another option – particularly when Madrid need a focal point in the final stages of matches. His early impact suggests he deserves more opportunities to show what he can do. Defend transitions better The other major concern is what happens when Madrid lose the ball. Atletico repeatedly found space around Madrid’s midfield and were able to attack quickly, while Huijsen’s red card made the situation even more difficult. If Mourinho wants his side to press aggressively and commit numbers forward, Tchouameni and Valverde must provide enough protection when possession is lost. Against Atletico, Denzel Dumfries, Ibrahima Konate, Huijsen and Marc Cucurella lined up in front of Thibaut Courtois. There is quality in that back four, but Mourinho will want greater cohesion – particularly when Madrid’s full-backs push forward. Courtois’ performance showed how important he remains, with the goalkeeper making several important saves to keep Madrid in the game. The aim for Mourinho will be to reduce those situations and make Madrid harder to expose when attacks break down. The veteran Portuguese needs to come up with some new answers to his team’s problems quickly, or there may not be much of a title race.

items.title: Maroc – Israël : colère dans la rue marocaine après l’accord sur les ambassades
items.description: L’humiliation de trop. Jeudi, la délégation marocaine n'a pas boycotté le discours du premier ministre israélien Benyamin Netanyahou à l’ONU alors que la plupart des pays ont quitté la salle. Dès le lendemain, les Marocains ont investi la rue. La normalisation avec Israël ne passe toujours pas auprès de l'opinion marocaine. Alors que Rabat et Tel-Aviv ont convenu mercredi 15 septembre d'ouvrir des ambassades respectives et d’échanger des ambassadeurs, les Marocains sont de nouveau sortis dans la rue pour exprimer leur rejet de la normalisation et leur soutien à la cause palestinienne. Vendredi 25 septembre, des milliers de Marocains ont manifesté dans tout le royaume. Des rassemblements ont eu lieu dans plusieurs villes et la manifestation la plus imposante est celle qui a eu lieu en soirée à Marrakech. Marche imposante à Marrakech contre la normalisation avec Israël Des milliers de manifestants ont battu le pavé dans la ville touristique, scandant des slogans contre le rapprochement avec Israël et l'échange d’ambassadeurs entre les deux pays. La manifestation a eu lieu sous le slogan “Vendredi de soutien à Al-Aqsa et contre la normalisation des relations avec le régime d'occupation”. C’est la deuxième manifestation du genre qui a lieu à Marrakech en quelques semaines, après celle de fin août dernier organisée pour protester contre la visite dans la ville de la ministre israélienne des Transports, Miri Regev, pour un séjour privé. Hier, à Marrakech, une manifestation de masse a eu lieu sous le slogan « Vendredi en soutien à Al-Aqsa et contre la normalisation des relations avec le régime d'occupation ». pic.twitter.com/OYsSckATeS — Liberté Свобода (@Liberte2050) September 26, 2026 Dimanche dernier, c'est la population de Tanger qui s'est soulevée pour dénoncer les nouveaux pas franchis dans le rapprochement avec Israël. Une grande manifestation contre la normalisation a eu lieu dans cette ville du nord du Maroc malgré la répression qui a marqué une précédente action. 76 rassemblements dans plus de 45 villes dans tout le Maroc , le peuple marocain a un message clair : Rupture immédiate de la normalisation avec l’entité sioniste et soutien sans faille au peuple palestinien pic.twitter.com/Jww05tmmk4 — Christophe Frot (@FrotChristophe) September 25, 2026 Discours de Netanyahou à l’ONU : l’humiliation de trop La reprise des actions de rue contre la normalisation survient alors que le Maroc et Israël ont franchi le dernier pas vers une normalisation totale de leurs relations en annonçant, mercredi 16 septembre, un accord pour relever leurs représentations diplomatiques au rang d’ambassades avec échange d'ambassadeurs. La grande manifestation de Marrakech est intervenue au lendemain d’une énième humiliation infligée par le Makhzen au peuple marocain. Jeudi 24 septembre, 77 délégations ont quitté la salle lorsque le Premier ministre israélien Benyamin Netanyahou s'apprêtait à prononcer un discours devant l’Assemblée générale de l’ONU. Parmi les délégations des pays arabes, seules trois n’ont pas quitté la salle. Il s’agit de celles du Maroc, des Émirats arabes unis et de Bahreïn. Ces trois pays ont normalisé leurs relations avec Israël en 2020 dans le cadre les accords d'Abraham. L’article Maroc – Israël : colère dans la rue marocaine après l'accord sur les ambassades est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Hundreds throng EducationUSA College Fair in Kumasi in pursuit of abroad studies
items.description: The EducationUSA College Fair in Kumasi witnessed yet another mass participation of students from secondary and tertiary levels in a bid to seek assistance for educational endeavors in the United States of America. With over 20 US-based universities and colleges present at the fair, over 3,000 prospective applicants sought information and assistance in their pursuit for higher learning overseas. The applicants are guided through the admission, visa and scholarship processes to the country, offering them deeper insights and prudent means to pursue their tertiary education. The advisers from EducationUSA work closely with students individually and in groups, in-person and virtually to enhance understanding of the college or university application process to be successful applicants. Executive Director of ACE Consult, Marilyn Owusu, highlighted how the event helps patrons build confidence and establish valuable connections. “As these students interact with the universities, it builds their confidence and give them the connections. So, when they are applying to the schools, they know what exactly they want,” she said. Over the last year, advisers from both the Accra and Kumasi centres have helped thousands of Ghanaian students apply to admissions across hundreds of accredited institutions of higher learning. Ghana, is currently the second highest sender of students in Sub-Saharan Africa to the United States, after only Nigeria with over 12,800 students studying across all 50 States in the United States, putting the country at the 14th place globally. “Education is important to us. The position of Ghana in terms of their travels to the US for education reflects how essential education is to the country for national development,” Pam De Volder, Public Affairs Officer at the U.S. Embassy, noted. The Ashanti Regional Minister, Dr. Frank Amoakohene noted that the region is seeking stronger educational exchanges and institutional partnerships to promote knowledge-sharing and build a global academic community. He says higher education should transcend national borders and facilitate knowledge transfer across countries. “Beyond EducationUSA, we are looking for more of educational exchange and institutional partnerships so that we can learn from each other in building a global community. Higher learning shouldn’t be bound by the boundaries of countries. We should be able to encourage knowledge transfer beyond borders,” he noted.

items.title: La production de la grenade tunisienne en hausse de 8%
items.description: La production de la grenade en Tunisie a connu une croissance globale remarquable entre 2010 et 2026, hissant le pays parmi les 10 premiers producteurs mondiaux. Cette filière est passée d ’ un statut de culture traditionnelle à celui de secteur agro-industriel hautement stratégique. La production est passée de 70 000 tonnes en 2016 à 106 000 tonnes en 2021 avec l’entrée en production des jeunes vergers. Pour cette saison 2026, les estimations affichent un net redressement de 8 % avec 98 000 tonnes attendues . La saison d’exportation des grenades tunisiennes débutera le 29 septembre courant pour les variétés locales, avec l’adoption d’un prix de référence évolutif, actualisé au fil de la saison en fonction des conditions du marché ainsi que de l’offre et de la demande. Tarek Tira, sous-directeur du développement des exportations au Groupement interprofessionnel des fruits (Gifruits), a déclaré à l’agence Tap que la fixation de cette date faisait suite à une réunion de travail tenue avant-hier, jeudi, au siège du groupement. Cette réunion a rassemblé la Direction générale de la production agricole, des représentants des Commissariats régionaux au développement agricole (CRDA) des principales zones de production, ainsi que des représentants de la profession. La détermination de la date de commercialisation à l’exportation de ce fruit a été décidée après le suivi des indicateurs de maturité et de coloration des grenades, et en coordination avec les différentes parties prenantes. Concernant la nouvelle récolte de grenades, le responsable a indiqué que la production nationale a atteint 98 000 tonnes, contre 91 000 tonnes l’année précédente, soit une hausse de 8 %, et ce, malgré une réduction de 15 % des superficies cultivées — une baisse principalement attribuée aux facteurs climatiques ayant affecté le secteur. M. Tira a précisé que les exportations de grenades ont atteint, au 31 décembre 2025, un volume de 9 791 tonnes pour une valeur avoisinant les 34,3 millions de dinars, contre 11 459 tonnes exportées à la même date en 2024 pour une valeur de 29,7 millions de dinars ; cela représente un recul de 15 % en termes de volume, mais une augmentation de 16 % en termes de valeur. Le porte-parole a indiqué qu’il a été convenu, lors de la réunion susmentionnée, d’élaborer un programme de promotion de la grenade sur le marché intérieur. Ce programme prévoit la création de supports publicitaires et d’un spot promotionnel pour la grenade tunisienne en arabe et en français, accompagnés de sous-titres en anglais. Par ailleurs, le groupement participera au Salon international de l’investissement agricole et de la technologie (Siat), prévu du 28 au 31 octobre 2026, ainsi qu’à diverses manifestations régionales et locales liées à la filière de la grenade, notamment le Festival de la grenade de Testour, le Festival de la grenade de Kettana et le Salon international des développements agricoles et hydrauliques de Gabès. Il a également été convenu d’organiser des activités de promotion de la grenade tunisienne et de ses dérivés en marge de la journée de présentation du salon MacFrut , prévue pour le 20 octobre 2026, au Rimini Expo Centre, en Italie, ainsi que de lancer une campagne d’affichage pour faire connaître la grenade tunisienne et ses atouts. Concernant le programme de promotion internationale de la grenade tunisienne, M. Tira a indiqué qu'une participation au salon Sial à Paris est prévue du 17 au 21 octobre 2026, l’objectif étant de renforcer la présence de la grenade tunisienne et de ses produits sur les marchés internationaux et d’établir des relations avec des opérateurs économiques et des importateurs. Un accord a été conclu avec les différentes parties prenantes pour participer au salon international Fruit Attraction à Madrid (Espagne), du 6 au 8 octobre 2026, afin de faire connaître et de promouvoir la grenade tunisienne, ainsi que d’explorer de nouvelles opportunités commerciales. Par ailleurs, des activités d’animation et de promotion seront organisées sur le marché italien — notamment aux marchés de gros de Rome et de Milan — pour stimuler la demande et faire découvrir aux professionnels et aux acheteurs les caractéristiques et la qualité du produit tunisien. Une campagne d’affichage sera également déployée au point de passage de Ras Jedir (sud-est) à la frontière avec la Libye pour promouvoir la grenade tunisienne et renforcer sa visibilité auprès des consommateurs et des opérateurs économiques, en particulier durant le pic de la saison. Il convient de noter qu’en 2025, la Tunisie a exporté des grenades vers une dizaine de pays à travers le monde. I. B. items.title: Drug bust: NACOC should be part of port inspection team – Twum-Barimah
items.description: The Deputy Director-General of the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC), Alexander Twum-Barimah, has called for the Commission to be included in teams responsible for inspecting containers entering and leaving Ghana’s ports. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, Mr Twum-Barimah argued that NACOC’s involvement was necessary to strengthen efforts to detect and prevent narcotics trafficking, particularly as containers are often loaded outside the port before being transported into the country’s ports. His comments come amid recent drug busts and renewed calls for stronger measures to prevent Ghana from being used as a transit point for illicit drugs. He questioned why authorities would limit the number of agencies involved in port inspections without including the institution specifically mandated to deal with narcotics. “Why aren’t we interested in ensuring that everything that is inside the container leaving your jurisdiction is clean?” he asked. Mr Twum-Barimah said although limiting the number of agencies involved in inspections may be intended to facilitate trade, narcotics control should remain a priority. He argued that NACOC should be included in the inspection arrangement because the other agencies involved do not have the same specific mandate to apprehend narcotics. “Even if you are limiting agencies for purposes of facilitating trade, in my own wisdom, I will tell you that an agency such as Narcotics Commission should never…” he said. He added, “Which of them had the mandate to apprehend narcotics? None. FDA doesn’t have role with narcotics, GSA, Customs doesn’t have any role with narcotics, so why wouldn’t you attach an agency such as Narcotics Control Commission to such a team?” Mr Twum-Barimah further proposed that even where authorities opt for a single inspection team to streamline operations at the ports, NACOC should be represented. “Even if it is going to be one team standing, it should be NACOC,” he said. NACOC ‘institutional gaps’ addressed The NACOC Deputy Director-General also disclosed that the Commission had undertaken internal efforts to address what he described as significant institutional gaps affecting its operations. He said the Commission had, over the past two years, worked to strengthen its institutional position and ensure that it is properly integrated into Ghana’s security and intelligence architecture. “The point is that we have behind the scene done a lot of work on this issue, having been in office for almost two years,” he said. According to him, the Commission inherited an institution with several gaps which, in his assessment, had weakened its effectiveness in narcotics control. He said NACOC had previously been excluded from important security structures despite its mandate to combat narcotics-related offences. “NACOC was not part of anything under their tenure, not even part of the regional and district security council,” Mr Twum-Barimah said. He also raised concerns about the Commission’s exclusion from the framework created under Ghana’s Security and Intelligence Agencies Act. According to him, although the legislation was enacted in 2020, NACOC was omitted from the relevant security architecture. “Meanwhile, it was 2020 that they made the law on Security Intelligence Act. When they were enacting that Act, deliberately, they omitted NACOC,” he said. Mr Twum-Barimah said the issue had since been addressed. “We had to fix that problem. Today, now it is fixed. A lot has been done,” he added. He maintained that closer integration of NACOC into port inspection and national security structures would strengthen the country’s capacity to identify and intercept narcotics before they enter or leave Ghanaian territory.

items.title: Ward appointed Liverpool’s sporting director
items.description: Liverpool have appointed Julian Ward as the club’s new sporting director. Ward, 45, replaces Richard Hughes, who held the role for just over two years before leaving in September. This will be Ward’s second stint as sporting director at Anfield, having first done the job during the 2022-23 season. He said he was “incredibly excited” to take on the role. Ward joined Liverpool in 2012 as European scouting manager for Spain and Portugal and was promoted to assistant sporting director in 2020. He succeeded Michael Edwards two years later but by November 2022, it had been confirmed that Ward would leave at the end of that season. Ward was brought back in 2024 as Fenway Sports Group’s technical director when Liverpool ‘s owners made Edwards their chief executive of football – and has been responsible for overseeing player development pathways and the academy for the past two years. FSG president Mike Gordon said: “We are delighted that Julian has agreed to take over leadership of our football operations department at this juncture, primarily because it is a role for which we believe he is the ideal candidate given his extensive experience of the football industry in general and Liverpool Football Club in particular. “The knowledge and expertise he brings will only enhance our football operations, while also ensuring Andoni Iraola is provided with the support he requires as he continues to make such a positive impression as head coach.” Ward appointment designed to bring stability – analysis Julian Ward’s appointment gives Liverpool ‘s hierarchy some much-needed stability after a summer of transition. Ward has done the sporting director job before – and bar a spell between the summers of 2023 and 2024, has been at the club since 2012. Liverpool did speak to external candidates but Ward was seen as the stand-out choice. One source described him as: “Calm, well-spoken and with a clear opinion and vision.” Ward’s previous spell as sporting director came under Jurgen Klopp, where he oversaw the signings of Luis Diaz, Cody Gakpo, Alexis Mac Allister and Darwin Nunez – he has a global contacts network and plenty of experience when it comes to negotiations. He was also influential when Mohamed Salah renewed his contract in 2022 – flying to see Salah on holiday to seal the deal – and his relationship with the agent Jorge Mendes helped Liverpool in their pursuit of Diogo Jota. There will be plenty of jobs for Ward to tackle – including the securing of Rio Ngumoha on a long-term deal now that he is 18 and determining whether new contracts are offered to Alisson and Virgil van Dijk before their current agreements expire this summer. As FSG’s technical director, Ward played a role in Liverpool ‘s push to recruit younger talent. And he has a good relationship with Mike Gordon, who oversees the day-to-day running of the club. Under Klopp, Ward left 12 months into a three-year deal, but should have more of a say now, given how the head coach role has been structured under both Arne Slot and his successor Andoni Iraola. Time will tell if Ward’s appointment proves successful – but in the here and now, he looks a more-than-sensible choice.

items.title: How Militarizing the Triumphal Arch Could Backfire for Trump
items.description: Donald Trump’s vision for a monumental arch in the nation’s capital was always ambitious. He has called for a 250-foot structure clad in granite, with gilded winged statues, an observation deck, a café, a gift shop, and an exhibition space—all to be completed by the end of his second term. And that was before he decided that the “triumphal arch” should also be a military complex. Since the project was announced last year, the Trump administration has raced to begin work on the memorial, checking many of the boxes required of a major new building project in D.C. It cleared one key panel, the Commission of Fine Arts, which Trump has stacked with loyalists. It got a sign-off from the Federal Aviation Administration (which has called for a “non-standard eternal flame” on the arch so that pilots can see it at night). Although the project still faces a lawsuit filed by veterans and a preservationist, this week an obscure independent federal agency terminated the project’s ongoing historic-preservation review—an unusual move that pushes the arch significantly closer to final approval. It may get that in November from the National Capital Planning Commission, another federal body that has rubber-stamped several of Trump’s building projects in D.C. Trump initially made little secret of the actual purpose of the arch, which will rise above Memorial Circle, a traffic roundabout between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. When a model of the structure was first spotted in the Oval Office last October, Trump told journalists that it was meant to honor “me.” After that, however, officials pitched it as a commemorative work for the nation’s 250th birthday. Later, in arguing against the veterans’ lawsuit, the project’s lead agency, the National Park Service, said the arch did not need congressional approval because a 1925 law had already authorized a pair of columns on that end of Memorial Bridge, to symbolize the post–Civil War reconciliation of North and South. Then, on Sunday, Trump invoked national security, announcing that the structure would house ammunition, drones, and snipers. “There will be no facility like this anywhere in the World,” he wrote on Truth Social. “Out of the 59 top cities and Capitals, Washington, D.C., IS THE ONLY ONE IN THE WORLD THAT DOES NOT HAVE A TRIUMPHAL ARCH, but it will now and, by far, the greatest of them all!” A White House official told me that the arch would include military infrastructure while also remaining open to the public, and that the newly announced features do not alter the design or review process. The National Park Service and Interior Department did not respond to my questions about the project. If changing the purpose of the arch was meant to speed construction, it could have precisely the opposite effect. The project was already in its final stages of approval, the pesky matter of the lawsuit notwithstanding. But Trump’s plan to deck out the arch with weapons is likely to involve more agencies, lead to more litigation, and—this might be the important part to Trump—create further delays. On Thursday, the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation announced it had ended the arch’s routine consultation process—known as Section 106—after the National Park Service concluded that it was unlikely to produce an agreement with outside parties providing feedback on the proposal. Although this process isn’t legally binding, officials undertake it for federal construction projects that could affect historic properties, and proponents say it forces agencies to evaluate the effects of their projects and allows the public to have a say. But it can take years. In this case, it took months before officials ended the process early. Outside parties are supposed to give feedback during the review, but Charles Birnbaum, founder of the Cultural Landscape Foundation, told me his group and other consulting parties were invited to only one meeting. Just days before the president’s announcement on Sunday, Park Service officials sent the consulting groups a proposed memorandum of agreement that acknowledged the arch would unavoidably harm surrounding historic properties, but that concluded the project would move forward as planned. Because the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation has now canceled this process altogether, it will prepare its own formal comments and seek approval from Interior Secretary Doug Burgum. That timeline means that the Trump administration could bring the arch before the National Capital Planning Commission in November. Sara Bronin, a former chair of the ACHP and a professor at the George Washington University Law School, told me that termination of consultation is very unusual and reserved for cases in which parties who have diligently worked to resolve a project’s adverse effects still fail to come to an agreement. During her year as chair, she said, she exercised that authority only one time (for a wind-energy project). “By prematurely terminating consultation on the Triumphal Arch proposed by President Trump, the ACHP and interim chair Travis Voyles are making a farce of the Section 106 process,” she wrote me in an email. “True consultation has never occurred for the Triumphal Arch, and it looks like the Park Service and ACHP will bend over backwards to avoid it.” [ Read: The rush-job presidency ] In theory, Bronin said, the arch’s expansion to include national-security infrastructure should actually trigger a new Section 106 process. Previously, the National Park Service determined that the structure would adversely affect historic properties. But that analysis was conducted for a triumphal arch—not a military facility. Greg Werkheiser, an attorney at Cultural Heritage Partners and a plaintiff in a lawsuit to stop Trump’s plans to paint the Dwight D. Eisenhower Executive Office Building, said the changing function makes the arch a fundamentally different undertaking from the one preservationist groups have reviewed. “That’s likely to be a legal problem,” he told me in an email. All of this comes after ACHP announced plans to water down the historic-preservation rules that have applied to the arch—which could mean that the next time the Trump administration wants to erect a new monument, it faces less red tape to begin with. The process for creating new monuments in Washington, D.C., is well understood. But adding drones and ammo to one is a new wrinkle. “There’s no American monument that’s ever been used for that on a permanent basis,” Bryan Clark Green, a former member of the National Capital Planning Commission, told me. If the arch is to double as a military facility, Green said, the government would need to rethink how people and vehicles enter the site, how military personnel move through the structure, and how the public is kept away from sensitive operations. All of those considerations would require major revisions that would bring the project back before the National Capital Planning Commission and the Commission on Fine Art. Green told me the new arch plans should also trigger another review from the Federal Aviation Administration, which released a final report a week ago determining that the structure “would not pose a hazard to aircraft” even though it sits near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport. Along with the “eternal flame,” floodlights have been ordered by the agency to illuminate the structure. The FAA did not respond to questions I sent the agency. The bureaucratic requirements won’t end there. Military construction ordinarily follows its own yearslong planning and budgeting process, involving the Pentagon, the White House, and Congress. Mark Cancian, a retired Marine Corps colonel who oversaw military-construction budgets for the federal government, told me that he would expect the Department of Defense to contribute at least some money toward military-use portions of the arch—which was already estimated to have a $100 million price tag. The president has claimed that the new changes were a “strong request” from the military. In response to questions I sent, DOD directed me to Trump’s Truth Social post that announced the plans. [ Tom Nichols: Trump’s monumental obsession ] Patrick Suermann, a Texas A&M construction-science professor and retired Air Force officer, was skeptical that the project Trump described is even realistic. “There’s a lot of things that don’t make it very feasible,” he told me. Some of the biggest obstacles are logistical. The arch would have to accommodate each of the military functions Trump named, Cancian said. Snipers would need suitable positions atop the structure, and ammunition would require secure storage. Suermann pointed to the military’s quantity-distance requirements, which are invisible safety boundaries intended to protect people and sites surrounding where explosives are stored. “If you have full-time ammunition stored there,” he said, “you have quantity-distance arcs that would make it impossible for anybody to ever go near it.” Again, the proposed site is a traffic circle that’s notorious for congestion during rush hour. In its draft agreement last week, the National Park Service said the project’s location in Memorial Circle was “central to the undertaking” and that relocating the arch would mean it’s not the same project anymore. Trump and his critics disagree on the appropriateness of putting a celebratory arch in the somber shadow of Arlington Memorial Cemetery. But the case for a military installation there is even less clear. There are no federal buildings to guard, the site’s proximity to the airport could potentially complicate drone operations, and it’s also not well suited for snipers. “The two lines of fire they have are really down the Mall or back at Arlington Cemetery,” Green said. “So exactly what is the threat?” If anything, the arch could become more of a target. In deploying his national-security logic, Trump may be hoping to strengthen his case in court, after that argument helped him, to a moderate extent, with his ballroom. With that project, a judge who ordered an aboveground work stoppage allowed subterranean construction to continue because of its military purpose. But there is no established requirement for any kind of military presence in Memorial Circle. Beyond the practical and the procedural challenges , the military additions sharpen a symbolic tension that has surrounded the arch project. Veterans and military families had already objected to the plans, which they said would dishonor fallen soldiers buried at Arlington National Cemetery, disrupt funeral processions and personal visits, and alter the solemn character of the memorial corridor, given that the arch would block the view from the cemetery to the Lincoln Memorial. Paul Eaton, a retired Army major general and senior adviser for the veteran-advocacy group VoteVets, described the project to me as “sacrilegious” and said the monument—which would be the tallest arch in the world—would cast a literal shadow over thousands of graves. “This is not something that the United States does,” he told me. Eaton’s objection is also personal. His father was killed in Vietnam and is buried at Arlington, and he and his wife visit the cemetery whenever they are in Washington. “It is hallowed ground,” he said. Earlier this month, he appeared in a VoteVets video campaign to mobilize more veteran families against the arch. The effort is also supported by Home of the Brave, a political-advocacy group whose leadership is made up of Democrats and Republicans—including former National Security Adviser Susan Rice and former Representative Barbara Comstock. Senator Jeff Merkley, the top Democrat on the Senate appropriations subcommittee that oversees federal parks, plans to introduce legislation next week that would block federal funding for the arch. The opposition to the project coincides with growing pushback to Trump’s plans for Washington’s landmarks. He has implied several times that the Kennedy Center may need to be demolished—a possibility that might have seemed absurd if not for Trump’s teardown of the White House East Wing last October. Trump’s arch plans are forcing critics to take another far-fetched scenario seriously: the possibility of gunfire from a tourist destination on the Potomac River. At the least, Birnbaum, of the Cultural Landscape Foundation, told me he imagines a surreal experience for visitors: “Turn right for the gift shop and turn left for the arsenal.”

items.title: PDP accuses APC of propaganda over Obasanjo’s 2027 Senate eligibility
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) House of Assembly candidate for Abeokuta South Constituency II, Hon. Adeoye Adewale Adeniran, has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of spreading misinformation and political propaganda over the eligibility of Senator Iyabo Obasanjo to contest the 2027 Ogun Central Senatorial election. Adeniran, in a statement made available to Vanguard in Abeokuta, described reports claiming that the Supreme Court had disqualified Obasanjo from contesting the election as “misleading, legally speculative and politically motivated.” He urged members of the public to disregard the reports, arguing that the Supreme Court judgment being cited in support of the claim neither mentioned Obasanjo nor contained any order barring her from contesting the election. His reaction followed the Supreme Court’s judgment of September 24, 2026, in a case involving the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and the Zenith Labour Party (ZLP) over provisions of the Electoral Act 2026, where the apex court upheld the validity of the disputed provisions and set aside an earlier judgment of the Court of Appeal which had voided them. The provisions in contention included Sections 77(5), 77(6), 77(7) and 84(2), which principally relate to party membership registers and methods of candidate nomination. Adeniran, however, maintained that the judgment did not name Senator Obasanjo or make any order disqualifying her from participating in the 2027 Ogun Central Senatorial election. “The attempt to present that judgment as an automatic disqualification of Senator Prof. Iyabo Obasanjo from the 2027 Ogun Central Senatorial election is factually unsupported, legally speculative and clearly designed to create confusion where none exists,” he said. He argued that the case before the Supreme Court arose from a dispute between INEC and a political party, stressing that Obasanjo was not a party to the proceedings. “It is therefore mischievous and intellectually dishonest to transform a judgment in a dispute between INEC and a political party into a purported judicial pronouncement against a particular candidate who was neither a party to the suit nor the subject of the judgment,” Adeniran stated. The PDP candidate challenged those circulating the alleged disqualification to identify the specific portion of the Supreme Court judgment that mentions Obasanjo or contains an order preventing her from contesting the election. According to him, the judgment dealt with the interpretation and application of specific provisions of the Electoral Act 2026 and did not constitute a ruling against Obasanjo’s candidacy. “What exists is a Supreme Court judgment on the constitutionality and operation of specified provisions of the Electoral Act 2026. This, however, has nothing to do with our candidate, who has never ceased to be a member of the PDP. “What does not exist is a Supreme Court judgment disqualifying Senator Iyabo Obasanjo.” Adeniran further alleged that the controversy was an indication of growing concern within the APC over the political profile of the PDP ahead of the 2027 general elections. He alleged that the APC had resorted to what he described as propaganda after recognising that political arguments alone could no longer contain the PDP’s growing acceptance across the state. The PDP candidate said the party’s candidates at various levels, from the governorship to the State House of Assembly, were prepared to offer residents of the State an alternative to what he described as years of hardship under the APC administration. He said the party’s campaign would go beyond political slogans, with its candidates expected to present policies and programmes targeted at addressing challenges confronting residents. Adeniran said the PDP’s agenda would prioritise economic opportunities, infrastructure, education, healthcare, employment, security and support for businesses and vulnerable citizens. According to him, the party’s candidates are determined to harness Ogun State’s human and material resources, expand opportunities for residents and restore public confidence in government. He added that the PDP was committed to providing what he described as purposeful leadership anchored on a clear vision and practical development plans for the state. The post PDP accuses APC of propaganda over Obasanjo’s 2027 Senate eligibility appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: This isn’t the first cocaine bust; NPP must stop the politicisation – NACOC deputy boss
items.description: The Deputy Director-General of the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC), Elexander Twum-Barimah, has urged the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) to stop politicising the recent seizure of cocaine in France linked to Ghana. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, September 25, he said this was not the first time authorities had intercepted cocaine or other illicit drugs at the country’s exit or entry points. “For us as a country, this has not been the very first time we have seen this. We have a large amount of cases on narcortics,” he noted. Mr Twum-Barimah said Ghana had recorded numerous drug seizures in the past and cautioned against treating the latest case as a partisan issue. “In 2018, 56 kilogrammes of cocaine were intercepted in Ghana; here, in 2019, the same. 2020, 3rd September, at the airport, we had someone bringing in an amount of heroin from Kenya,” he noted. Watch the full conversation below. The remarks follow the seizure of nearly 3.9 tonnes of cocaine by French customs at the port of Dunkirk. The drugs were reportedly concealed in a container of plastic waste shipped from Ghana. Six people have appeared before a court in Accra in connection with the case. The NPP has called for the removal of heads of state agencies responsible for port security, customs and narcotics control, arguing that the shipment raises serious questions about how drugs could leave Ghana undetected.

items.title: Sénégal-Azerbaïdjan : une nouvelle dynamique dans les relations bilatérales
items.description: Un mémorandum d’entente instituant des consultations politiques a été signé entre le Sénégal et l’Azerbaïdjan à l’occasion de la Semaine de haut niveau de la 81ᵉ session de l’Assemblée générale des Nations Unies. L’information a été donnée le vendredi soir par le ministère de l’Intégration africaine, des Affaires étrangères et des Sénégalais de l’extérieur. À l’occasion de la Semaine de haut niveau de la 81ᵉ session de l’Assemblée générale des Nations Unies, Cheikh Niang, le ministre de l’Intégration africaine, des Affaires étrangères et des Sénégalais de l’Extérieur, a signé avec son homologue azerbaïdjanais un mémorandum d’entente instituant des consultations politiques entre le ministère des Affaires étrangères de la République d’Azerbaïdjan et le ministère de l’Intégration africaine, des Affaires étrangères et des Sénégalais de l’Extérieur. Ce mémorandum établit, selon une note du ministère, un cadre régulier de concertation entre les deux pays, destiné à favoriser le dialogue politique et à approfondir leur compréhension mutuelle sur les questions d’intérêt commun. M. DIEME

items.title: Tanger : mandat de recherche contre Mounir Limouri sur fond de suspicions de fraude électorale
items.description: Un mandat de recherche a été émis à l'encontre de Mounir Limouri, maire de la ville et responsable provincial du Parti Authenticité et Modernité (PAM), dans le cadre d es investigations menées autour des irrégularités enregistrées lors du scrutin du 23 septembre 2026 à Tanger, ont indiqué à Hespress des sources bien informées. Cette mesure intervient alors que des informations ayant largement circulent indiquent le Limouri aurait quitté le territoire national, avant d'être rejoint par les membres de sa famille proche. L'annonce de cette procédure à l'encontre du président du conseil communal de la ville du Détroit a provoqué de vive réactions dans les milieux politiques locaux. Ces développements s'inscrivent dans le cadre de l'enquête judiciaire ouverte sous la supervision du parquet compétent suite aux incidents survenus au bureau de vote de l'école Al Qods, situé dans le quartier populaire de Casabarata. À ce stade, cinq personnes ont été placées en garde à vue, tandis que les investigations se poursuivent sous un suivi rigoureux des autorités supérieures afin de faire toute la lumière sur ce dossier. L'affaire a éclaté dès les premières heures du scrutin lorsque des tensions ont émergé autour de l'établissement scolaire Al Qods. La découverte d'un sac contenant des bulletins de vote pré-cochés en faveur du PAM a entraîné l'interpellation immédiate d'un suspect sur place, suivie de la diffusion sur les réseaux sociaux d'une vidéo montrant des enveloppes suspectes dans une urne. Le procureur général du Roi près la Cour d'appel de Tanger a rapidement ordonné l'ouverture d'une enquête judiciaire afin d'établir les responsabilités pénales. Face à ces accusations, la direction du PAM a rejeté ce qu'elle qualifie de campagne de dénigrement orchestrée. Abdelatif Ghelbezouri, tête de liste du parti dans la circonscription de Tanger-Assilah, arrivé en troisième position, a réfuté tout lien entre sa formation et l'individu interpellé. Il a précisé que sa présence dans les locaux de la préfecture de police visait à déposer une plainte pour diffamation et non à répondre à une convocation des enquêteurs. The post Tanger : mandat de recherche contre Mounir Limouri sur fond de suspicions de fraude électorale appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: 2027: More appointments, structures coming — ADC campaign council
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike The African Democratic Congress, ADC, Presidential Campaign Council has said that more appointments and campaign structures are expected as it continues to build its national organisation ahead of the 2027 elections. The council said the list of appointments already released was only an early stage of the exercise, with more senior positions and structures still to be announced as consultations widen across the country. In a statement on Saturday by its Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the council said the latest appointments were significant to the campaign’s organisation but did not represent its final composition. “The campaign is still evolving. Consultations are continuing, and further responsibilities will be assigned as the structure expands across the country,” Shaibu said. The clarification also appeared aimed at supporters and political allies who may have expected their names to feature in the first list, with the campaign stressing that years of loyalty and sacrifice had not been overlooked. “To those who may feel disappointed that their names have not appeared yet, we ask for patience and understanding. No one should believe that years of commitment and sacrifice have been forgotten,” Shaibu said. He said the campaign would draw on party loyalists, experienced leaders, professionals, young people and other Nigerians prepared to contribute to its work. Shaibu said the next phase would include the announcement of zonal and state structures, additional senior appointments and organisational structures extending to wards and polling units nationwide. “Our strength has always been our people and the relationships built over many years. We must preserve that bond,” he said. The campaign is also putting together a policy structure focused on issues directly affecting Nigerians, including the cost of living, food security, agriculture, security, energy, jobs, industrialisation, manufacturing and small businesses. Other areas listed by the council include education, healthcare, infrastructure, housing, public finance, governance, technology and innovation, social protection, natural resources, the environment and human capital development. Shaibu said the policy framework would seek to connect the different challenges rather than treat them as separate problems. “Nigeria’s challenges are interconnected and cannot be addressed in isolation. The objective is to ensure that every major national problem is matched with a serious, practical and implementable policy response capable of improving the everyday lives of Nigerians,” he said. He said the campaign would continue to expand around Nigerians willing to participate in its political and policy work. “This is a people-driven national campaign. It will continue to grow organically, drawing strength from Nigerians who share the desire to build a country where life is more affordable, businesses can thrive, young people can find opportunity and families can once again look to the future with confidence. “There is room in this journey for every sincere hand willing to serve,” Shaibu added. items.title: RCCG’s $265,854 donation funds evacuation of 100 Nigerians from S’Africa
items.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has evacuated 100 Nigerians from South Africa with funding from a $265,854 donation by the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG) for the purchase of one-way tickets for 500 distressed Nigerians seeking to return home over xenophobic and Afrophobic attacks. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed this in a statement on Saturday, adding that another five returnees were evacuated with funding from a private Nigerian citizen, bringing the latest batch to 105 Nigerians. The returnees, comprising 82 adults and 23 children, arrived in Lagos aboard South African Airways Flight SA060 on Thursday, September 24, 2026, at approximately 8:30 p.m. They were received by officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Nigerians in Diaspora Commission (NIDCOM), the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and other relevant Federal Government agencies. The ministry said Nigeria’s diplomatic mission was continuing engagements with the leadership of the RCCG in South Africa, as well as other philanthropic groups and individuals, to facilitate the evacuation of more Nigerians in distress. It added that some other Nigerians seeking evacuation were undergoing preliminary clearance with the Nigerian Consulate in Johannesburg and relevant South African authorities. They would be evacuated once the necessary processes had been completed. The latest arrival represents the 13th consular evacuation from South Africa since the exercise began on June 10, 2026, bringing the total number of Nigerians evacuated to 1,821. The statement in parts, “It is important to note that the return of 100 persons in this batch was funded from the Two Hundred and Sixty-Five Thousand, Eight Hundred and Fifty-Four US Dollars ($265,854.00) donation made by the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG) towards the purchase of one-way tickets for the evacuation of 500 distressed Nigerians from South Africa. The return of the remaining five was funded by the generous donation of a private Nigerian citizen. “Nigeria’s diplomatic mission continues to engage with the leadership of the RCCG in South Africa and other philanthropic groups and individuals, as some other distressed Nigerians are currently undergoing preliminary clearance with our Consulate in Johannesburg and relevant South African authorities. “They will be evacuated as soon as the process is finalized. Of this number, the Federal Government fully funded the evacuation of 1,388 Nigerians.” The Federal Government expressed appreciation to the RCCG, under the leadership of Pastor Enoch Adejare Adeboye, for its donation towards the evacuation of 500 distressed Nigerians. It also acknowledged other groups and individuals who had supported efforts to bring Nigerians facing distress and safety concerns in South Africa back home. The ministry said the contributions demonstrated the impact of collaboration between public institutions, religious organisations and private individuals in addressing humanitarian challenges. The Federal Government expressed concern over persistent xenophobic and Afrophobic attacks against Nigerians and other Africans in South Africa. It said it remained committed to diplomatic efforts and other concrete measures to secure the cooperation of South African authorities in addressing the attacks and ensuring the safety, security and dignity of Nigerians living in the country. The government also assured Nigerians in the diaspora that protecting their lives, rights and welfare remained a priority, adding that appropriate diplomatic and consular measures would be deployed to assist them whenever necessary. It urged Nigerians residing in South Africa to remain vigilant, law-abiding and maintain contact with the Nigeria High Commission in Pretoria and the Consulate General of Nigeria in Johannesburg for consular assistance whenever required. items.title: 'Largest hypocrisy in the world': Pakistan tells UNGA India’s 'terrorist exports' have gone global
items.description: Pakistan on Saturday accused India of having “elevated propaganda into statecraft”, embraced disinformation as diplomacy and “exported terrorism as an instrument of policy”, as Islamabad hit back at remarks made by the Indian representative at the UN General Assembly. In a reply to the Indian representative’s statement during the general debate of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, Counsellor Saima Saleem termed India a state “that has elevated propaganda into statecraft, embraced disinformation as diplomacy, exports terrorism as an instrument of policy, pursues hegemony as a regional strategy, mainstreamed Islamophobia and institutionalised Hindutva ideology”. “The extraordinary balance sheet of today’s incredibly intolerant India. It exports terrorism and violence while trying to import victimhood and sympathy,” she said. “Pakistan knows the cost of Indian-sponsored terrorism all too well,” she said, adding that since the turn of the century, Pakistan had lost nearly 100,000 lives to terrorism, generations had been scarred and billions of dollars had been drained from the country’s economy. She said Pakistan’s counter-terrorism efforts and sacrifices had been well recognised internationally. “We have also presented to the international community extensive evidence of India’s financing, aiding and abetting of terrorist groups targeting Pakistanis, including the TTP, BLA and Majeed Brigade,” she said. “Yet, despite its endless lectures to others on terrorism, we are still waiting to hear India unequivocally condemn the terrorist attacks that kill innocent Pakistani civilians. But how can we expect India to condemn its proxies?” she stated. She said India’s “terrorist exports have gone from regional to global”, citing former Indian naval commander Kulbhushan Jadhav, convicted in Pakistan on terrorism and espionage charges, and Nikhil Gupta, who pleaded guilty in the United States for plotting the murder of a Sikh leader at the direction of the Indian government. She also referred to “others implicated in assassinations carried out in Canada”. Kashmir dispute Turning to the Kashmir dispute, the counsellor said: “Jammu and Kashmir never was, neither is, nor will ever be an integral part of India. It is an internationally recognised disputed territory, a huge part of which is under India’s forcible and illegal occupation for nearly eight decades against the wishes of the Kashmiri people, and in gross violation of international law and numerous resolutions of the Security Council.” “The contrast between AJK and Indian-occupied Jammu and Kashmir could not be more stark,” she said. “In AJK, Kashmiris enjoy rights, participate in political life and have the freedom to express their opinions, while the people of Indian-occupied Kashmir endure decades of occupation, repression and denial of their fundamental rights and freedoms, including the inalienable right to self-determination. Rights exercised cannot be equated with rights denied,” she said. ‘Largest hypocrisy in the world’ Saima said the ruling RSS-BJP dispensation in India had “institutionalised Hindutva ideology in state policy and practice, and unleashed a reign of terror against minorities”. “Muslims are demonised; Christians persecuted; Dalits dehumanised; and Sikhs disenfranchised in the largest hypocrisy in the world,” she said. She said massacres of Muslims in Gujarat and Delhi under state patronage, calls for the genocide of Muslims, Islamophobic rhetoric by politicians and discriminatory citizenship laws were part of the “Hindutva project”. Indus Waters Treaty On the Indus Waters Treaty, Saima said that by the “so-called holding in abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty and blatantly disregarding its international legal obligations, including the sanctity of treaties”, India had “stooped to a new low of weaponising water, a lifeline for the 240 million people of Pakistan”. She said India’s “false narratives and disinformation could not hide the crushing defeat it suffered at Pakistan’s hands during Marka-i-Haq in May 2025 ”. “It is well recognised by the international community that India lost more than a military conflict; it lost its credibility. Today, India can no longer import sympathy as it stands exposed in front of the world,” she said. “As stated by my prime minister, Pakistan remains steadfast in its pursuit of peace, mutual respect, dialogue and the peaceful settlement of disputes in our region and beyond — a commitment reflected in our consistent role as a peacemaker, mediator and bridge-builder,” she stated. “We will defend ourselves whenever aggression is imposed upon us, but we will never abandon the path to peace; for lasting strength lies not in the wars a nation can fight, but in the peace it has the courage to build and defend.” Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday said any attempt by India to stop, impede or divert Pakistan’s share of water would be treated as an “act of war”. Addressing the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York, he said India’s decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance had no legal basis, adding that the country’s position had been rejected by UN experts and the Permanent Court of Arbitration.

items.title: Tourisme au Bankui-Sourou : « Il faut accompagner les projets viables et faire confiance aux acteurs », soutient Lansané Dao,
items.description: Le développement du tourisme passe aussi par l'accès au financement. Pour Lansané Dao, président de la Fédération régionale des acteurs du tourisme de Bankui-Sourou (FRAT-B), les acteurs ont besoin de mécanismes de financement adaptés, de davantage de souplesse et d'un accompagnement permettant de moderniser les infrastructures et de valoriser les sites touristiques. Dans cet entretien, il revient également sur les atouts touristiques de la région et les défis qui se posent au développement du secteur dans le contexte actuel. Lefaso.net : Pouvez-vous présenter à nos lecteurs la fédération que vous présidez ? Lansané Dao : La Fédération régionale des acteurs du tourisme de la région de Bankui-Sourou (FRAT-B) regroupe six provinces, à savoir les Balé, les Banwa, le Mouhoun, la Koosin, le Sourou et le Nayala. La fédération est une organisation professionnelle qui a pour mission de fédérer, de représenter, de professionnaliser et de promouvoir l'ensemble des acteurs du tourisme de l'espace Bankui-Sourou afin de structurer une offre touristique intégrée, de renforcer la compétitivité des entreprises, de valoriser les patrimoines et de contribuer au développement économique des territoires. Notre vision est de faire du tourisme burkinabè un secteur professionnel, compétitif, inclusif et durable, porté par des acteurs unis et engagés, contribuant au développement économique, social et culturel des territoires et au rayonnement du Burkina Faso. À l'horizon 2030, nous voulons faire de l'espace Bankui-Sourou une destination touristique intégrée, attractive, professionnelle, inclusive et durable, portée par des acteurs unis et innovants, et contribuant au développement économique, culturel et social des territoires. Combien de membres compte la fédération ? Pour l'instant, elle a été constituée sur initiative du ministère en charge de la Culture et du Tourisme. Dans chaque région, le processus a été lancé au mois d'août et il est toujours en cours. Mais nous avons été l'une des premières structures à être mises en place, le 17 août dernier. Quelles sont les potentialités touristiques de votre région ? Les potentialités sont nombreuses. Je peux dire que nous avons une destination à découvrir. Lorsque vous partez de Boromo, vous traversez trois ponts historiques qui relient différentes parties du Burkina Faso. Si ces ponts rencontraient des difficultés, c'est une grande partie du pays qui serait affectée. Ils sont donc très importants. Il y a notamment le pont du Mouhoun construit à l'époque de la colonisation, un pont intermédiaire réalisé sous le président Sangoulé Lamizana, puis le dernier pont construit sous la présidence de Roch Marc Christian Kaboré. Ce sont des ouvrages historiques qu'il faut préserver et moderniser pour les générations futures. Nous avons également Boromo, qui est une destination incontournable, avec la forêt des Petits Balé et la forêt des Grands Balé, qui abritent de nombreux animaux, notamment des éléphants. Nous avons même un éléphant apprivoisé, appelé Nani, qui permet aux enfants et aux visiteurs de découvrir cet animal emblématique. Toute la population de Boromo connaît Nani. Par zone, nous avons aussi de nombreuses potentialités : la poterie de Tchériba, la fosse à hyènes de Ouroubonon située dans la zone de Boromo, Toma île, qui est une véritable destination à découvrir. Il y a également les constructions en hauteur dans la zone de Barani. Nous disposons donc de nombreux sites à valoriser. La région de Bankui-Sourou est représentée à cette 16e édition du SITHO par une délégation de 18 personnes Nous avons aussi élaboré un répertoire regroupant les hôtels, les restaurants et, à terme, les maquis de la région. L'objectif est de développer un outil numérique permettant à toute personne souhaitant visiter notre région de localiser facilement les sites touristiques, les hébergements et les services disponibles. Disposez-vous de statistiques sur les visites des sites touristiques de la région ? Pour l'instant, je ne peux pas donner de statistiques, car ce sont des données qui sont encore en cours de collecte. La région a été fortement affectée par la crise sécuritaire. Comment les acteurs du tourisme ont-ils fait preuve de résilience ? Le simple fait d'être présents ici montre que nous existons toujours. Nous ne voulons pas nous laisser affecter par cette crise dont l'objectif est de nous étouffer et de freiner notre développement. Nous devons donc faire preuve de résilience. Les acteurs du tourisme sont convaincus qu'il faut continuer à travailler malgré les difficultés. La paix reviendra et il faut préparer l'avenir dès aujourd'hui. Nous pouvons dire qu'il existe beaucoup de potentialités et de nombreuses initiatives. Nous pensons que bientôt cette crise sera derrière nous. Quels sont les principaux défis rencontrés par les acteurs du tourisme ? Il y a beaucoup de difficultés. La première est l'accès au financement. Sans accompagnement, il est difficile de développer les infrastructures et les activités. Ensuite, il y a la formation professionnelle des acteurs. Il faut aussi travailler à la valorisation des sites touristiques et à l'amélioration des voies d'accès. Les difficultés sont donc d'ordre financier, structurel et infrastructurel. Existe-t-il des projets en cours pour améliorer l'accessibilité des sites ? Pour le moment, il s'agit surtout de plaidoyers auprès des autorités afin que ces préoccupations soient prises en compte dans les futurs projets. Il n'y a pas encore de travaux engagés dans la région. Que pensez-vous de la thématique du SITHO consacrée au financement des projets structurants ? Le financement doit s'accompagner d'un assouplissement des conditions d'accès aux ressources. Il ne suffit pas de mettre en place des mécanismes si les acteurs ne peuvent pas remplir les critères exigés. Nous souhaitons davantage de souplesse, des lignes de crédit adaptées et des mesures d'accompagnement permettant aux porteurs de projets de concrétiser leurs idées. Le secteur touristique est principalement porté par le privé, dont les ressources sont limitées. Il faut donc une volonté politique forte, notamment à travers des mesures de détaxation, des critères de financement adaptés et des lignes de crédit spécifiques au secteur. Et une fois qu'on sent qu'un projet est viable, c'est vrai, on peut prendre des risques, mais il faut l'accompagner, parce qu'il peut vous étonner. Un artiste, c'est quoi ? C'est quelqu'un qui crée. Et si vous n'arrivez pas à avoir confiance en lui, déjà, même avec beaucoup de conditions, ça peut le démotiver et même l'empêcher d'arriver au résultat. Le premier problème, c'est qu'il faut avoir confiance en lui. Donnez-lui l'argent, il va vous le rendre avec le résultat. C'est un peu ça que nous demandons. Le directeur général de Faso Tourisme, Sulaïman Kagoné (en bleu) a effectué un tour au stand de la fédération Avez-vous le sentiment que le tourisme interne progresse aujourd'hui ? Oui. Aujourd'hui, c'est le tourisme endogène qui fait vivre les acteurs du secteur. Les touristes étrangers sont moins nombreux, mais les Burkinabè redécouvrent progressivement leur patrimoine. Dans les hôtels, sur les sites touristiques et dans les espaces culturels, ce sont de plus en plus les visiteurs nationaux qui occupent les lieux. C'est un signal encourageant. Vous allez voir les chiffres à la fin, vous allez comprendre que les gens ont pris conscience que le tourisme, c'est nous qui devons travailler à le développer. Donc, je pense que ce sont déjà de bons signaux. Que le gouvernement continue dans ce sens-là, en nous accompagnant et en nous faisant confiance. Vous allez voir que nous n'avons même pas besoin que des gens viennent d'ailleurs. Nous, en interne, on peut travailler à valoriser et à développer notre industrie touristique. La question de la qualité, de l'accueil et du confort est souvent évoquée quand on parle de tourisme. Des actions sont-elles prévues en ce sens ? Le ministère travaille actuellement à la structuration des acteurs autour de plusieurs filières professionnelles. Les fédérations régionales sont mises en place et une confédération nationale des acteurs du tourisme devrait voir le jour. ''Nous avons tout ce qu'il faut chez nous'', soutient Lansane Dao Des orientations sont données pour renforcer la professionnalisation du secteur. Mais, encore une fois, la question du financement demeure essentielle. Si les acteurs disposent des moyens nécessaires, ils pourront améliorer leurs infrastructures et respecter davantage les normes. Aujourd'hui, tout le monde a compris que c'est à nous de développer notre tourisme. Nous n'avons pas besoin d'attendre que d'autres viennent le faire à notre place. Lorsque l'on prend l'exemple du Kenya ou de l'Éthiopie, on voit que le tourisme peut être un moteur de développement. Pourquoi pas chez nous, alors que nous avons du potentiel ? Lorsqu'on souhaite que les hôtels respectent certaines normes, il faut nécessairement mettre à leur disposition les moyens financiers nécessaires. Avec un financement adapté et assorti de certaines conditionnalités, les établissements pourront mieux respecter les normes exigées. Cela leur permettra également de se mettre à niveau, aussi bien sur le plan administratif que dans leurs pratiques professionnelles, afin de renforcer la confiance des clients. Je pense donc que l'accompagnement, notamment en matière d'accueil et de qualité des services, est essentiel pour permettre au secteur de progresser. Si vous deviez convaincre quelqu'un de visiter les Bankui, que lui diriez-vous ? Le Bankui-Sourou est une destination à ne pas manquer. C'est une région à très fort potentiel touristique. C'est le grenier du Burkina Faso. Qu'est-ce que cela signifie ? Cela signifie qu'avant d'entreprendre quoi que ce soit, il faut bien être à jour de son ventre avant d'avancer. Donc, nous avons tout ce qu'il faut chez nous, non seulement en matière de céréales et d'agriculture, pour pouvoir faire les transformations nécessaires et mettre ces produits à la disposition de nos visiteurs. Nous avons également une grande richesse culturelle, avec de nombreux masques traditionnels : les masques bobo, les masques de Dédougou, de Toma, les masques de Ouri, de Boromo et d'autres localités, chacune ayant ses spécificités. Vous pouvez également découvrir les éléphants, les crocodiles, Toma île, les constructions en hauteur, ainsi que les anciens pièges à hyènes de Ouroubonon, qui témoignent du savoir-faire des populations locales pour se protéger de la faune sauvage. Il y a véritablement beaucoup de choses à découvrir dans les Bankui. Un mot de fin ? Je voudrais vous remercier pour l'intérêt que vous portez à notre région. Cet accompagnement nous rassure, nous donne davantage de visibilité et encourage les acteurs du tourisme à poursuivre leurs efforts, car nous pouvons encore faire beaucoup de choses. Merci au camarade président du Faso, Ibrahim Traoré. Entretien réalisé par Fredo Bassolé Lefaso.net
